author: Kevin Kelly
short: Permission diffs, category routing, and reliable event delivery.
description: Log messages, reactions, server/thread changes, members/presence, voice activity, scheduled events, and bot commands with configurable switches and channel routing. Use [p]log or /log settings, plus direct logstatus/logchannel/lograte controls. Add channel/role permission diffs, category routing, editable channel exemptions, bounded delivery retries/status, uncached message events, and guided setup. Add opt-in retained local history, member timelines, text/category/date searches, and JSON/CSV exports with automatic retention.
install_msg: Load with [p]load logplus, then use [p]log setchannel #channel. See the cog README for permissions, command names, and current limitations. Enable slash commands as the bot owner with [p]slash enablecog logplus, then [p]slash sync. Use [p]log setup for guided settings and [p]log delivery to inspect failures.
end_user_data_statement: This cog stores per-guild event settings, log destination channel IDs, source/category routing overrides, retry preferences, exemption channel IDs, and style/rate preferences in Red Config. Optional local history persists event timestamps, type/category/source IDs, identified member IDs, titles, descriptions, and fields, including message text. It starts disabled and retains up to 1000 events/2 MiB per server for 1 to 90 days. Discord log messages can contain user names and IDs, message contents, invite codes, and event details. These posted logs remain in Discord until removed there. Pending retry records temporarily hold event details/message contents in memory within queue and expiry limits. User-data export/deletion hooks return or remove pending and retained records containing the user's Discord ID; deletion also clears cached audit entries. Delivery counters are held in memory.
